about: MUTATING — writes a partition table and a filesystem, which is the most destructive thing any verb here does. STILL INERT, though the approval channel now exists (design 17835005, decided by David 2026-09-21 — a rendered plan, signed with his passkey, single-use, verified before the argv is built; the runner half landed with backlog fd7090cc): it declares requires_approval and names plan-a-disk-commission as its plan_verb, but its script takes no plan_sha256, so it cannot re-render the plan and refuse one that drifted since it was signed, and the runner refuses an approval verb that cannot (q4: drift voids an approval). It becomes usable when its script takes the hash as its last param, as reap-terminated-pods and merge-tenant-main do. Its bound is by construction of the ONE script it calls (infra/forge/commission-a-disk.sh): the target must be a /dev/disk/by-id/ path, must carry no partition table, must have nothing mounted on it and must not back the root filesystem, all re-checked immediately before the write rather than once at plan time. A kernel name is refused outright — on 2026-09-21 adding a disk to the forge renumbered the devices and the drive that looked like the new one by number was the one carrying the system.
